openings.claim: A return-to-home-screen step coupled with a visitor language choice before handoff could remove inherited language state and shorten menu navigation.
openings.delta: Treat menu readiness and requested language as joint handoff conditions alongside battery readiness.
openings.prediction: If inherited menu state causes delays, the pair may outperform resetting alone or advance choice alone; effects remain untested.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps, each step alone and existing practice across matched language requests. Stop if return handling exceeds 30 seconds on average.
assumptions: Reset returns reliably to the home screen.
Choice can be communicated without retaining visitor data.

openings.claim: Language-specific dock positions plus a visible menu-state check might reduce wrong-language handoffs by aligning location cues with actual settings.
openings.delta: Use location and verified setting together instead of charge indication as the availability cue.
openings.prediction: If location cues remain accurate, the pair may outperform dock grouping alone; uneven language demand could erase the benefit.
openings.probe: Compare paired steps with grouping alone under equal and uneven demand. Stop if admission work is delayed or visitor history is retained.
assumptions: Dock positions can be marked without replacement.
Setting checks do not consume admission capacity.
